claims: Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) is a chronic inflammatory skin condition.
HS causes painful, recurring lumps under the skin.
HS causes abscesses under the skin.
HS causes tunnels under the skin.
HS usually occurs in areas where skin rubs together such as armpits and groin.
HS is caused by clogged hair follicles.
HS is not contagious.
HS is not caused by poor hygiene.
Treatment for HS includes medications such as antibiotics, biologics, and steroids.
Treatment for HS includes surgery.
Symptoms of HS include small, pitted, blackhead-like areas.
Symptoms of HS include painful red lumps that increase in size and rupture.
Symptoms of HS include leaking abscesses.
Symptoms of HS include scarring.
Hurley Stage I (Mild) of HS consists of single or isolated lumps without sinus tracts or scarring.
Hurley Stage II (Moderate) of HS consists of recurring, separated lumps with some scarring and tunnel formation.
Hurley Stage III (Severe) of HS consists of multiple interconnected tunnels and abscesses across a large area.
The exact cause of HS is unknown.
HS involves hair follicle blockage.
Hair follicle blockage causes swelling and immune system overreaction in HS.
HS primarily begins after puberty.
HS often begins in the late teens or early 20s.
Obesity and smoking are significant factors that can trigger or worsen HS.
HS is more common in women.
HS often has a genetic component.
There is no cure for HS.
Treatments for HS include topical or oral antibiotics like clindamycin or tetracycline.
Treatments for HS include painkillers such as NSAIDs.
Treatments for HS include hormonal therapies.
Treatments for HS include oral retinoids.
Adalimumab can treat moderate-to-severe HS.
TNF/IL-17 inhibitors can treat moderate-to-severe HS.
Treatments for HS include surgical drainage.
Treatments for HS include laser hair removal.
Treatments for severe HS include excision of the affected skin.
